source_contracts.role: Fitted construction versus body-relative pattern placement
source_contracts.trace: prepare receives the actual DrapeInput, GarmentBuild, FitSettings and Fabric and constructs Fit from that same build. selection.is_fitted is a locally derived construction predicate: fitted geometry is already where worn, pattern geometry gets floor/pelvis translation and clear_panels. Canonical RigJointName L_UPLEG/R_UPLEG lookup produces RigJointOrdinal for the typed joint table; no primitive ordinal cast here. Local hip closure retains native eight-float joint-state row and reads translation x/z. Its unit/frame interpretation remains a qualified canonical owner question, not an additional joint identity owner.

GarmentPose::for_mesh makes one identity Move per mesh panel plus one whole garment Move. Pivots::of derives garment centre and per-panel particle range/centre from the same base mesh retained by Fit. place applies panel nudge about that panel pivot first, then whole-garment move, always against base positions. This prevents accidental cumulative placement from already moved output and separates garment versus panel responsibility despite shared Move representation. Default/short panel list deliberately supplies identity; no stricter count policy invented. Pairing ranges with their centres is a coherent local numerical helper record; no universal particle/panel index framework or duplicate pose owner proposed.

source_contracts.role: Translation, angular components, local panel and body-space frames
source_contracts.trace: Move documents offset in metres and yaw/pitch/roll in degrees around named body axes. apply maps pitch/yaw/roll to native XYZ degree vector, calls existing rotate_xyz, then adds pivot and offset. Exact rotate_xyz converts each component to radians and applies X,Y,Z in that order, matching pattern Placement::apply. These are meaningful unit/axis distinctions; raw Vec3 storage is used at this identified arithmetic port. It does not settle broader typed physical/angle/frame propagation or justify flattening named components, scaling body or changing transform order.

source_contracts.role: Body collider versus whole outfit collision surface
source_contracts.trace: collision_surface first copies input wearer geometry then appends each successful inner garment with vertex offset; triangles and vertices belong to this same constructed BVH. Fit.set_body receives only wearer geometry, installs collision mesh and retains body-only BVH for body-specific clear_body. If obstacles exist, set_collision_mesh replaces active collision surface with combined body/garments while body remains distinct. Shared TriangleBvh/Vec3 shape does not make these authorities identical. Actual drape782131 and saved788200 consume same returned combined collision surface; outfit78638 supplies successful prefix obstacles.

placed_positions invokes retained pose/base/pivots. clear_panels groups matching contiguous panel ranges, samples vertices/face centres, and chooses least required common shift along either normal; margin is settings.body_offset_cm*0.01 plus canonical fabric particle radius. Particle write receiving contract is retained from158. Fit.set_pose writes placed positions, stores pose and resets frame count. set_body invokes clear_body; that query uses original body BVH triangle/result mapping, explicit normals and metre offset before writing lifted positions. Collision receiver carries named body_offset_cm converted by CM_TO_M plus fabric friction into MeshSurface/MeshCollider. No whole-module raw primitive exemption or proof of all arithmetic/degenerate values.

source_contracts.role: Returned fit and collision surface tuple
source_contracts.trace: (Fit,TriangleBvh) contains distinguishable types with actual separate responsibilities; caller destructures them. A new wrapper would not prevent a demonstrated swap at this two-different-type boundary. Preserve same-build/same-input construction association rather than invent new IDs or broad equivalence claims.
